hint.text: A helping verb is a verb that comes before the main verb. It helps the main verb to show action or make a statement.

instruction.text: Select the helping verb in the sentence.

wrong.text: Called and eaten are the main verbs in this sentence because they show action. Look for a word that does not show direct action or make a statement itself.

atoms.b: When you called me, I ((had)) already eaten.
atoms.sound: When you called me, I had already eaten.

instruction.text: Select the helping verb in the sentence.

wrong.text: Telling is a main verb in this sentence because it shows action. Look for a word that does not show direct action or make a statement itself.

atoms.b: Mr Russell ((was)) telling us about his summer plans.
atoms.sound: Mr Russell was telling us about his summer plans.

instruction.text: Select the helping verb in the sentence.

wrong.text: Wonder and received are the main verbs in this sentence because they show action. Look for a word that does not show direct action or make a statement itself.

atoms.b: I wonder if he ((has)) received my email.
atoms.sound: I wonder if he ((has)) received my email.

instruction.text: Select the helping verb in the sentence.

wrong.text: Sell is the main verb in this sentence because it shows action. Look for a word that does not show direct action or make a statement itself.

atoms.b: At the school fair, we ((could)) sell cookies for a good cause.
atoms.sound: At the school fair, we could sell cookies for a good cause.

instruction.text: Select the helping verb in the sentence.

wrong.text: Was and know are main verbs in this sentence because they show action or tell us more about the subjects’ states of being. Look for a word that does not show direct action or make a statement itself.

atoms.b: We ((did)) not know that there was a construction site.
atoms.sound: We did not know that there was a construction site.

instruction.text: Fill in the gap with the correct helping verb.

atoms.b: ((++Have Did Are)) you talked to Sam?
David and his mother ((++will have is)) travel to New Zealand next year.
In spite of the rain, Lindsay ((++did is has)) not skip football training.
Mauricio ((++is will have)) cheering for his boyfriend’s team.
You ((are ++must have)) cook the chicken thoroughly.
You ((++may ++can have)) open the window if you want.
